# Adjust image hue

- Route: `/tools/adjust-image-hue`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `photo`
- Slug: `adjust-image-hue`

## Summary

Rotate every color in a photo by up to 180 degrees, or move only the reds, greens or blues, with a live preview and a full-resolution export. (Photo editing)

## Details

Hue is the angle of a color on the wheel, and this page opens Aperture, the Media Manipulator photo editor, with the Color (HSL) panel in front so you can turn that angle. The adjustment is one layer in the stack: every pixel is converted from sRGB to HSL, its hue is rotated by the All colors slider plus whatever the six range sliders add for that particular hue, and the result is converted back and clamped. Nothing is baked in. You can drag Hue to +30 to push teal water toward blue, see the change on the GPU preview at once, then export a file rendered from the original pixels on our server. A master shift of 180 degrees swaps every color for its complement; a range shift of 20 degrees moves one family and leaves the rest where it was.
### What it does
- The All colors Hue slider runs from -180 to 180 degrees and rotates every pixel by the same angle, so +120 turns red into green, -120 turns red into blue, and either 180 or -180 lands on the opposite side of the wheel.
- Six named ranges, Reds at 0 degrees, Yellows at 60, Greens at 120, Cyans at 180, Blues at 240 and Magentas at 300, each carry their own Hue, Saturation and Lightness sliders plus a Width and a Feather that decide how far the range reaches.
- The eyedropper adds a custom range centered on any color you click in the photo, up to 32 ranges in one layer, which is the way to target a specific orange or purple that falls between two named ranges.
- Range edits fade out on gray: a pixel with HSL saturation under 10 percent gets a proportionally smaller shift, so concrete, white walls and shadows do not take on a color cast when you move the Reds.
- The layer is non-destructive, with opacity, a blend mode, an optional mask and unlimited undo; you can stack a second Color (HSL) layer for a second family of colors and export when the preview looks right.
### How to use it
1. Open the photo: Drop a JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC, AVIF or TIFF into the box above. The editor opens full screen with Color (HSL) selected.
2. Choose master or range: Drag the All colors Hue slider for a global rotation, or pick Reds, Yellows, Greens, Cyans, Blues or Magentas and move only that range.
3. Tune width and feather: Widen a range to catch neighbouring hues or narrow it to isolate one, and set the feather so the edge of the shift is invisible.
4. Export: Pick JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or TIFF and a quality; the server re-renders the original at full size with the same hue math and names the file (retouched).
### Supported formats
- Input: JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC, HEIF, AVIF, TIFF, BMP
- Output: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF
- Hue rotation is a per-pixel operation in gamma-space HSL; the export of a 24 megapixel original takes a few seconds on the server and is paced by encoding, not by the math.
- HEIC, TIFF and BMP originals need an account because the server prepares the preview copy the browser cannot decode.
### Technical details
- For each pixel the hue h, saturation s and lightness l are taken in HSL. The output hue is h plus the master Hue plus the sum over ranges of weight times that range Hue; saturation is s multiplied by 1 + master Saturation/100 and by the product of 1 + weight times range Saturation/100; positive Lightness values move l toward 1 by amount times (1 - l) and negative ones move it toward 0 by amount times l. The result goes back to RGB and is clamped to 0..1.
- A range weight is 1 when the circular distance between the pixel hue and the range center is at most Width/2, falls in a straight line to 0 across the Feather, and is 0 beyond Width/2 + Feather. With the defaults of Width 30 and Feather 30, a range is solid 15 degrees either side of its center and ramps out to 45: hue 20 gets a Reds weight of 0.833, hue 30 gets 0.5 from Reds and 0.5 from Yellows, and hue 45 belongs entirely to Yellows. Width accepts 10 to 120, Feather 0 to 90.
- Every range weight is multiplied by min(1, s / 0.1), the neutral fade. A pixel at HSL saturation 0.04 receives only 40 percent of a range shift; a pixel at 0.1 or above receives all of it. The master Hue is not faded, but a true gray has zero saturation and comes back as the same gray whatever angle you add, and a near-gray at 4 percent saturation changes only by a few levels.
- Hue is circular, so Reds at center 0 cover both sides of the seam: a pixel at hue 350 is 10 degrees from the Reds center and gets the full Reds weight, and a shift that pushes a hue past 360 wraps around to the start of the wheel.
- The preview is drawn on your graphics card in WebGL2 from a 1920 px proxy of the photo; the file you download is rendered by our server from the original pixels with the same HSL formulas. The two agree within the documented tolerance for color operations, a mean error of at most 1 and a maximum of 4 levels out of 255.
### When not to use it
A hue slider is the wrong tool when the whole photo is tinted by the light it was shot in: that is a white balance problem, and the temperature and tint sliders on our white balance page correct it in linear light without pushing hues past each other. It is also the wrong tool for changing one object while a same-colored object elsewhere must stay: hue ranges select by color, not by position, so add a Brush or Radial mask or use the object color page. Pure desaturation belongs to the saturation page, and converting to monochrome belongs to the black and white page, where the six channel sliders decide the gray of each hue.
### Use cases
- Correct water and sky: Tropical water that came out teal moves toward blue with a Cyans Hue of +20 to +30 while the sand, which has almost no cyan in it, stays put.
- Warm or cool foliage: A negative Greens Hue pushes leaves toward yellow for an autumn feel; a positive one pushes them toward cyan for a cooler, wetter look.
- Recolor a product: Pick the product color with the eyedropper, set the custom range Hue to the angle you need, and leave Width and Feather small so nothing else moves.
- Creative color swaps: A master shift of 180 degrees gives a complement-swapped frame in one move; smaller master shifts give the cross-processed look of shifted film.
### FAQ
Q: What is the difference between the All colors Hue and a range Hue?
A: All colors adds the same angle to every pixel regardless of its color. A range Hue adds its angle only to pixels whose hue falls inside that range, scaled by the range weight and faded out on near-gray pixels, so it moves one family of colors and leaves the others untouched.
Q: Why does a small hue change look so large on some colors?
A: Hue is an angle, and the perceived step per degree is not uniform around the wheel. Between yellow and green a few degrees is obvious; between blue and violet the same step is subtle. Watch the preview and use the histogram rather than aiming for a particular number.
Q: Will shifting the Reds affect skin?
A: Yes, usually. Skin tones sit around hue 15 to 30, inside the Reds range and partly inside Yellows, so a Reds Hue change moves skin too. Add a Color range or Brush mask to the layer to keep faces out of it, or narrow the Reds Width so the range stops before the orange skin hues.
Q: Why did my gray background not change when I rotated the Reds?
A: Range shifts are multiplied by min(1, saturation / 0.1). A gray background has saturation near zero, so its weight collapses to zero and it keeps its tone. That is deliberate: hue edits on neutrals would add color casts you never asked for.
Q: Can I rotate the hue of a color that sits between two named ranges?
A: Click it with the eyedropper to create a custom range centered on its exact hue, then give that range its own Hue, Width and Feather. Up to 32 ranges fit in one Color (HSL) layer.
Q: Does a hue shift change the brightness of the photo?
A: Not in the HSL model the editor uses: lightness is held constant while the angle turns. Perceived brightness still differs between hues, so a yellow rotated to blue will look darker even though its HSL lightness is identical. The live histogram shows the luma change if you want to compensate with the Lightness slider.
